section: Closing strips and fillers for Maxima and Intarsio
source_pages: printed p.434 / PDF 436 (subset extracted: the H.60 row of the third position)

filler_wall_unit.description: Wall unit filler in door finishes from 2,3 to 15 cm - with one-piece bottom

front_layout.note: One finished front covering the whole face. NO hinge_axis and no mechanism - A FILLER DOES NOT OPEN, so 70_symbols draws no leaf, which is the same treatment a US appliance panel gets: it too states a single front it never swings. The kind is STATED rather than left absent because Panel.effective_slabs and Panel.gola_options both default a missing layout to 'single', and a default is not a source. It also means the front shortens to 750 with the rest of the run when the door version is gola - a filler's front line must meet its neighbours' or the drawing breaks.

filler_wall_unit.notes: THIS IS THE ARTICLE THE FIVE-CENTIMETRE CLOSING-STRIP RULE HAS BEEN ASKING FOR. printed p.11: 'If a rh or lh wall unit with a "D" handle is installed adjacent to a tall unit or a wall, it is advisable to fit a closing strip of at least 5 cm so that the wall unit can be fully opened.' wall_h60.json records that the rule bites on PD0131, PD0531 and PD0631 and that we had nothing to fit; PD0151 is the thing, and 50 mm sits inside its 23-150 range. THE POLICY DOES NOT CHANGE: warn, never auto-insert. printed p.10-11 carry FIVE such rules, not one - claude/fillers-recon-2026-08-23.md lists them, and all five turn on the grip system or the handle model, so they belong with the other restrictions waiting on M1.6.
